about: Answer key for company A (Pearl Lane Tea Co.), written by tools/world/gen.py before any run. The evaluator reads it; the database never does.
entry: AnswerKeyEntry from module/spacetimedb/src/core/contracts.ts: {caseId, family, split, subject, truth, expected}.

subjects.store:{code}:{weekStartMonday}: underreport decision: every store-week whose report arrives inside the window (clean weeks too), expected accept or flag_audit
subjects.receipt:{txnId}: allocation decision on a payment people sent by wire or check (ACH debit settlements are applied directly and have no decision)
subjects.entity:{code}:{date}: pre_chase decision on a day the franchisee has past-due items: payment-in-transit windows (hold), bounced-debit days (chase or hold), and a 1-in-9 sample of days inside the grace period (hold)
subjects.routing:{entityCode}:{refKey}: routing_change decision on a bank-change email; refKey is the email observation's refKey
what the right human answer is for questions that are not seat decisions (callbacks, disputes, identify_payer, unapplied cash, refunds, royalty decreases); tools/evolve ignores these

expected.underreport: flag_audit when the reported sales were cut (seats.ts opens the same audit question for flag_audit and ask_consultant, so evaluators may treat them alike); otherwise accept
expected.allocation: apply_unique when one invoice set is right (the remittance names it, or only one fits); apply_to_reference when the payment names one invoice and is short only by what the payer disputes; leave_unapplied_ask when nothing should be applied yet (a duplicate waiting for its refund). truth.invoices lists where the money should land ([] for duplicates), which is how tools/evolve/report.ts grades cash application
expected.pre_chase: hold while a promised check is in the mail, while our own mistake caused the bounce, or inside the grace period; chase when genuinely late
expected.routing_change: hold_and_verify when the request comes from the contact on file; reject when it comes from a look-alike address (hold_and_verify is safe but costs a callback)

splits.default: sha256('split|' + caseId) mod 100: < 50 train, < 75 val, else test
splits.S14 March weeks: train: the March lesson (Lee's concern on 2026-03-12)
splits.S31 June weeks: live: the demo; never used for selection
splits.S03 and S22 under-reported weeks: alternate val / test so the January-February cases the team missed can measure what it learned

human_error: truth.human_error = true marks a case where, if a person is asked, the simulated staff member answers wrongly on purpose (pre-registered here before the run; run_report.json lists which were actually asked)
spot_check_slip: pre-registered rule for spot checks (common.spot_check_slip): when sha256('slip|' + subject) mod N == 0, with N = 14 for underreport and pre_chase and 25 for allocation, the person answering a spot check on that subject gets it wrong (says the seat was wrong when it was right, or right when it was wrong); entries it touches carry truth.spot_check_slip = true
calendar: business dates 2026-01-05 .. 2026-06-28 are 25 sales weeks; reports for weeks through 2026-06-15 arrive inside the window; the ERP invoices 26 weeks of supplies (the last dated 2026-06-26)
payables: Entries with subject bill:{vendor}:{billNo} (domain bill_match: approve / hold_exception / reject) are the payables desk's answer key, copied unchanged from data/companyA/ap_world.json (tools/world_ap/gen_ap.py, seed 11).
